challenge.better_approach: Alternative: only rename on Windows (os.name branch). Rejected - two spellings of one store re-creates the divergence being fixed (same as the commons-path ticket); one spelling everywhere, legacy read tolerated. Alternative: mkdir per-skill subdir 'skill/idea.jsonl' - changes the store shape for every glob reader; heavier.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That block names contain ':' only as the 'skill:' prefix and the mapping ':'->'__' cannot collide with a real block name; that no external consumer (Linux dial, sleep cycle) globs the colon name - to be censused in the build; that legacy files are only on Linux/other boxes.
challenge.prior_art: Consulted congruency-lab: learning_block charter owns the trace; nothing about filename portability. git grep: 5 hand-built spellings of '<block>.jsonl' (learning_block.py:101,144; clearance.py:251; three skill probes; engine_trace_corpus glob). On this box the failed write left an empty file named 'skill' in traces/ - NTFS treated 'skill:idea.jsonl' as an alternate data stream of 'skill'.
challenge.real_collision: None found: no intention pins the trace filename; Law 7 (records of truth never collapse errors) is respected because the legacy file is folded, not dropped.

answers.falsifier: On Windows, firing /idea, /intent and /sorted writes traces with no WinError 87; on a seeded legacy 'skill:intent.jsonl', intent_door_refusals counts the same passes/refusals before and after the rename; reverting the writer makes the proof fail.
answers.from_idea: none, because /idea itself fails on NTFS (WinError 87 writing skill:idea.jsonl in cairn/machines/learning_block/learning_block.py), measured on akiendell 2026-11-12
answers.how: One public function in learning_block (trace_path / trace file name) maps a block name to a filename with ':' replaced; write_trace writes the new name, folds any legacy colon file into it and retires the legacy file at the write; read_trace reads legacy + new. The three skill door-refusal probes (intent, sorted, saveslate) that build 'skill:<x>.jsonl' by hand move onto read_trace; clearance.py:251 builds QUEUE_BLOCK.jsonl by hand and moves onto the same function; engine_trace_corpus globs *.jsonl and keys by path.stem, so it must key by the record's block field or de-mangle the stem. Proof: a hollow writer fails on a ':' block name under a Windows-reserved-char check, and a reader proof seeds a legacy colon file and a new file and asserts both are counted.
answers.traces_to: Law 5 / Law 3: the corpus the dial and the refusal probes measure must be readable on every box; Law 1 - one function names a trace file instead of five hand-built spellings.
answers.what: learning_block writes a trace file whose name is legal on every box (no ':'), and every reader of those traces finds both the new name and the legacy 'skill:<name>.jsonl' files already on Linux.
